# Physics validation

`mrgym validate` runs 36 checks of engine `mrgym-engine-0.1.0`; all must pass, and the test suite asserts it. Each row compares the scanner with an analytic formula or with a calculation written separately from the engine.

What this establishes: the scanner computes the equations it states, to the bounds listed. What it does not: agreement with a measurement, with a real scanner or with another group's simulator. Rows whose reference was written by the same authors say so. References: [references.md](references.md). Simplifications: [limits.md](limits.md).

## Signal models

| # | Check | Reference | Measured | Bound | |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | Ernst formula, spoiled gradient echo | Ernst & Anderson 1966; separately written matrix Bloch steady state (bloch.py); an implementation check of the closed forms | 1.1e-16 | ≤ 1e-12 | pass |
| S2 | dual-TR (AFI) signals | Yarnykh 2007; separately written matrix Bloch steady state (bloch.py); an implementation check of the closed forms | 3.7e-16 | ≤ 1e-12 | pass |
| S3 | inversion recovery with a gradient-echo readout, inversion efficiency 0.8 to 1 | separately written matrix Bloch steady state (bloch.py); an implementation check of the closed forms | 3.3e-16 | ≤ 1e-12 | pass |
| S4 | flip angle of maximum spoiled-GRE signal | Ernst angle arccos(exp(-TR / T1)); Ernst & Anderson 1966 | 0.0009 deg | ≤ 0.005 | pass |
| S5 | RF-spoiled steady state (EPG) of spgr and afi, 8 cases | separately written isochromat-ensemble Bloch simulation (1,024 spins, time stepping) | 3.5e-12 | ≤ 1e-09 | pass |
| S6 | the same, and 3 cases with diffusion | separately written time-stepping EPG in the laboratory frame (same b-factor formula: checks the solver, not the diffusion model) | 4.9e-12 | ≤ 1e-09 | pass |
| S7 | EPG with RF phase increment 0, 100 cases | SSFP-FID closed form; Hänicke & Vogel 2003 | 4.3e-15 | ≤ 1e-10 | pass |
| S8 | EPG reduces to the ideal-spoiling formulas when T2 << TR, TR >> T2, or diffusion spoiling is complete | Ernst formula; AFI formula | 2.9e-14 relative | ≤ 1e-06 | pass |
| S9 | EPG differs from the Ernst formula where it should (TR 5 ms, 30 deg, T1 1500 ms, T2 200 ms) | incomplete spoiling at short TR and long T2 (Zur 1991; Preibisch & Deichmann 2009) | 7.8 % apart | ≥ 0.03 | pass |
| S10 | spin echo with imperfect pulses (B1 60 to 120 % of nominal) | separately written matrix Bloch chain; ideal pulses: 1 - 2 E(TR - TE/2) + E(TR) | 2.2e-16 | ≤ 1e-12 | pass |
| S11 | inversion-recovery spin echo, inversion efficiency 0.94 | separately written matrix Bloch chain | 0 | ≤ 1e-12 | pass |
| S12 | refocusing efficiency of a spin echo | sin^2(beta / 2); Hennig 1988 | 1.1e-16 | ≤ 1e-12 | pass |
| S13 | inversion-recovery null point for TR >> T1 | TI_null = T1 ln 2 | 4.1e-06 relative | ≤ 0.0001 | pass |
| S14 | balanced SSFP steady state, 200 random (T1, T2, TR, flip, off-resonance) | closed form (Freeman & Hill 1971; Scheffler & Lehnhardt 2003) against Bloch time stepping | 3.7e-06 | ≤ 0.0001 | pass |
